correctness.rationale: The inverse branch lengths add to the output length, giving a doubly stochastic transition matrix and the asserted uniform average of row entropies. In fact the stationary law is unique: full-branch cylinders shrink uniformly and map onto the interval, so every input cell contains a cylinder from which every output cell is reached along a positive-measure orbit segment, giving a positive-probability path in the resampled chain. In N-scaled coordinates, complete input cells have the given one-branch density, and shifting their index by s translates their images by the integer L, leaving entropy unchanged. When the turn is not aligned (equivalently L does not divide N by coprimality), the only leftover row is obtained by adding the two branch masses in each bin, not their entropies; both images are anchored at the integer output endpoint N, so the reflected bins and τ determine this row without any additional N dependence. Increasing N by L adds p and q full rows and keeps this row unchanged. This yields the exact recursion and all residue constants, including the aligned case N=L and N=1. Each full row has positive entropy because its image length is greater than one scaled output bin. An independent replay at (p,q,N)=(1,4,4), intersecting each input cell with clipped output-bin preimages [k/20,(k+1)/20] and [1−(k+1)/5,1−k/5] and multiplying by 4, gave rows (1,1,1,2)/5, (0,0,2,3)/5, (0,3,2,0)/5, (4,1,0,0)/5. The four full right-branch rows in a period contribute two binary entropies at each of 1/5 and 2/5, and the left gives log 5. This yields the stated H∞ and C_4=(2/25)log(32/27)>0, with C_1=−H∞<0. The fixed sign repeats by the exact recursion, not finite extrapolation. Frozen verification notes and verify.py were read, not executed; their broader finite checks do not prove the unrestricted statement.

value.rationale: This determines the signed leading discretization bias exactly in a standard expanding family and supplies a strict witness against one-sided or monotone convergence, in both directions infinitely often for the same map.
